question: During the autocompletion task, what did Copilot use to make its suggestions?
options: Code you had already typed
Comments in your file
Function and variable names
The assignment instructions on the course website
A request typed into a chat box
explanation: Inline completion needs no prompt. The code and comments around your cursor act as the prompt.

question: Which can Copilot use as context for its next suggestion?
options: Lines above the cursor
Lines below the cursor
Other files open in the editor
Every repository you have ever made
Your browser history
correct_answers: Other files open in the editor
explanation: Context is what's near the cursor and open in the editor. It is more than the current line, and less than everything you've written.

question: You write # return the average of the list above def avg(nums):. Then you change only the comment to # return the median. What happens to the suggestion?
options: It changes, because the comment is part of the context
It stays the same, because Copilot ignores comments
It stays the same, because Copilot remembers its first suggestion
Copilot asks which one you meant
correct_answers: It changes, because the comment is part of the context
explanation: Every edit changes the context, and the prediction is recomputed from it.

question: Copilot suggests a function using your variable ottoCartTotal, a name that exists nowhere on GitHub. What does this show?
options: It found an identical function in a stored repository
Another user wrote this exact code earlier
It generated new code by predicting it, using names from your file
It searched Google for a match
correct_answers: It generated new code by predicting it, using names from your file
explanation: Code that doesn't exist anywhere cannot be retrieved. The model builds new text piece by piece.

question: There are two correct solutions: a common but slower one and a rare but faster one. Which is Copilot more likely to suggest?
options: The fastest one, because it optimizes code
The shortest one
The one most similar to common patterns in its training data
The one your professor taught
correct_answers: The one most similar to common patterns in its training data
explanation: Copilot predicts what is likely, not what is optimal.

question: When did Copilot learn Python coding patterns?
options: Before release, by training the model on large amounts of public code
Each time you type, by comparing your code with other users' code
Engineers wrote rules for every function
By checking which users' code was correct and saving it
correct_answers: Before release, by training the model on large amounts of public code
explanation: Training happens once, ahead of time, on public code. The model does not keep learning while you type.

question: A Stack Overflow answer posted 10 minutes ago solves your exact problem. Will Copilot suggest that code?
options: Yes, it searches the web as you type
Yes, if the answer has many upvotes
No, it uses patterns learned during training plus your current code
Only if you paste the link into a comment
correct_answers: No, it uses patterns learned during training plus your current code
explanation: Copilot does not browse the web while you code. Its knowledge comes from training that happened before you used it.

question: You write a helper fmt_money() in one project. A week later you open a new, empty project. Will Copilot suggest fmt_money() there?
options: Yes, it saved your code to its memory
Yes, the model retrained on your code
No, it only sees the code currently open in your editor
Yes, if you accepted it many times
correct_answers: No, it only sees the code currently open in your editor
explanation: Your code is temporary context, not permanent memory. The model does not change while you use it.

question: Copilot suggests a pandas function that was removed in newer versions. Why?
options: It copied a broken Stack Overflow post it just found
Its training data contained a lot of older code that used that function
It optimizes for the shortest code
Another user's wrong code was stored and reused
correct_answers: Its training data contained a lot of older code that used that function
explanation: The model reflects the data it was trained on, including outdated patterns. It does not look anything up live.

question: Copilot suggests code that crashes when you run it. Why didn't Copilot catch the bug?
options: It ran the code but missed the error
It doesn't run or test code; it predicts code that looks likely
The server was down
Another user saved buggy code to its database
correct_answers: It doesn't run or test code; it predicts code that looks likely
explanation: Suggestions are never executed, so code that looks right can still fail.

question: Your code is correct, but your function is named process(x) with no comments, and Copilot suggests unrelated code. What is the most likely cause?
options: The server stored wrong code from another user
The name and code gave too little context to predict your intent
AI is randomly wrong some of the time
The system was down
correct_answers: The name and code gave too little context to predict your intent
explanation: Vague context leads to a vague guess. Clear names and comments are the human's part in getting good suggestions.
